rationale: The question I registered last turn is the only one in the index with no interpretation, and the remaining budget cannot carry a probe plus its reading, so I closed it from the sources and said so plainly in its limits rather than leaving a dangling registration or filing an experiment no turn could interpret. The mechanism is settled by reading: the lease test is force := bytes.Equal(m.GetContext(), []byte(campaignTransfer)) on a higher-term MsgVote or MsgPreVote, so a request carrying that marker is not ignored while the leader context is live; the receiver advances to the higher term, becomes a follower with no leader, and then applies canVote and isUpToDate. The marker is attached only by campaign() when t == campaignTransfer, the path reached from stepFollower's MsgTimeoutNow case, so a node campaigning normally never carries it and the lease keeps suppressing ordinary election traffic - which is the whole point of the design, since a leadership transfer must not be blocked by the lease. The judgment follows from that: the marker is a claim about the sender's own internal precondition, the receiver keeps no record to check it against, and the snapshot assigns it no verification duty, so this is the same byzantine-claim boundary the run already refuted for the term-less network message, not a second instance of the missing classification. It is recorded as explained with the defect claim refuted, and the empirical discriminator stays registered on the question so a future run can measure it in one probe. I also re-verified the whole record before closing: every receipt cited by any interpretation or knowledge entry exists, every cited index is inside its receipt's event count, and every cited source is a captured material - problems: none, with fifteen distinct receipts, thirteen questions and twenty-three knowledge entries, and no gaps.

interpretations.rationale: The question is answered yes on the mechanism and no on the defect, from sources only. The lease is written as force := bytes.Equal(m.GetContext(), []byte(campaignTransfer)) and the higher-term vote request is discarded only when force is false and inLease holds, so a sender that sets that context is answered: the receiver adopts the higher term, becomes a follower with r.lead = None, and then evaluates canVote, whose third clause (MsgPreVote with a term above the receiver's own) or its reset vote/leader state makes the grant available, subject to isUpToDate. The marker has exactly one producer in the snapshot: campaign() sets Context = []byte(campaignTransfer) when t == campaignTransfer, the campaign that begins in stepFollower's MsgTimeoutNow case via r.hup(campaignTransfer) and that increments the term and sends MsgVote at the new term. Two consequences follow and both matter for how the lease should be read. First, the bypass is narrow by construction: a node campaigning on its own, including a stale one that has lost contact with the leader, never carries the marker, which is why the lease still withheld the vote in every receipt of the main account. Second, the trust it places is in a statement about the sender rather than in anything the receiver holds: the receiving node keeps no record of a pending transfer and the context field is neither authenticated nor compared with local state, so it cannot tell a real transfer from a claimed one. That second point is what decides the judgment, and it is the same shape as the term-less network message this run already refuted: a sender claiming an internal precondition it does not hold is outside the crash-fault model the audit prioritises, and the snapshot states no duty for the receiver to verify a transfer it was told about. I therefore record the mechanism as a fact and the defect claim as refuted rather than asserted, with the empirical half left to the registered discriminator.

knowledge.assertion: The lease is skipped when the incoming vote request carries the CampaignTransfer context marker, and that marker is attached only by a transfer campaign, so ordinary election traffic is still suppressed by the lease.

counterevidence: The bypass does not help a candidate that is genuinely behind: after the term advance the receiver still applies canVote and isUpToDate, so the marker removes the lease delay for an already-eligible candidate rather than manufacturing support for a stale one.

The behaviour is deliberate rather than accidental: campaign() attaches the marker precisely so that a leadership transfer is not blocked by the lease it is meant to override, and the receiving side is designed to trust the leader's instruction that produced it.

A node that campaigns normally never carries the marker, so the lease continues to protect the incumbent against ordinary election traffic, which is what every receipt of the main account shows by measurement.
limitations: Source reading only: no execution delivered a request carrying the marker, so the mechanism rests on the cited branches rather than on a receipt, and the discriminator registered on this question is the probe that would measure it.

Relying on the bypass requires a sender that claims an internal precondition it does not hold, which is outside the crash-fault model; a source statement placing a verification duty on the receiver would reopen the refutation, and none has been found in the snapshot.
Config.CheckQuorum must be set for the lease to exist at all, so with it unset this bypass is moot rather than dangerous.
